title: Caldera Gaming — Performance Bridge Testplan & Run Notes
content:
One-line summary:
Caldera Gaming wants predictable sub-120ms p95 response for short chat intents (<=64 tokens) at 600 concurrent players per shard while keeping hosted cost under $0.45 / 1k tokens. This testplan captures the bridge evaluation we ran to reconcile latency SLOs, throughput caps, and cost tradeoffs between model variants and deployment shapes.

Context and goals:
- Customer: Caldera Gaming (fast-growing multiplayer title, heavy chat + in-game assistant usage).
- Primary workload: short interactive prompts (average tokens in/out ~48), occasional long diagnostics or session summarization requests (~800 tokens).
- Key SLAs: p95 <= 120ms for short prompts; p99 < 400ms preferred.
- Cost target: maintain average token unit economics <= $0.45 / 1k tokens for production mix.
- Environments tested: Dedicated (A100 80GB pool), Hosted (H100-backed instances in us-west), and a Low-cost variant (quantized L4-equivalent node).

Test matrix (high level):
- Models: redwood-13b-v2 (fp16), redwood-13b-q4f (4-bit), redwood-7b-v1 (fp16 cheaper), cached-redwood-13b-v2 (prefix caching enabled).
- Hardware targets: H100 (hosted), A100-80GB (dedicated), L4-sim (quantized cheaper).
- Sequence length buckets: short (<=64), medium (65-256), long (>256 up to 800).
- Concurrency sweep: 50, 150, 300, 600, 1200 concurrent sessions (synthetic client flows to emulate user think time).
- Batch sizes: continuous batching auto (runtime default), forced small-batch (1-4), forced large-batch (16-32) to measure tradeoffs.
- Cache states: cold (no K/V warm), warm (prefix cache preloaded for 70% of requests), mixed (30% warm).

Methodology notes (how we measured):
- Load generator: internal harness that replays real session traces recorded during closed beta (sanitized). Each virtual user cycles with a 2–8s think time distribution for short intent tests to keep the QPS realistic.
- Latency measurement: end-to-end from API ingress to token stream start (generation start) and full generation finish for longer sequences. Reported p50/p90/p95/p99.
- Cost calculation: tokenized by Redwood tokenizer; included GPU/hour cost estimates (hosted list price equivalent), amortized memory & infra overhead. Cost numbers are indicative for decisioning, not a billing forecast.
- Run cadence: each config ramped 30s warm, 10m steady-state sampling window, 3 repeats. We note variability as standard deviation across repeats.

Key results (short-intent focus, <=64 tokens):
- H100 hosted, redwood-13b-v2 (auto-batching + warm cache): p50=22ms, p95=98ms, p99=210ms, throughput at 600 concurrent ~92 req/s sustained. Cost estimate: $0.52 / 1k tokens (above target).
- A100 dedicated, redwood-13b-v2 (forced small-batch 4, warm cache): p50=28ms, p95=115ms, p99=270ms, sustainable at 600 concurrent with slight jitter during occasional cache miss spikes. Cost estimate: $0.40 / 1k tokens (meets cost target).
- L4-sim quantized redwood-13b-q4f (hosted cheap pool): p50=35ms, p95=145ms, p99=420ms. Throughput higher per-dollar but misses p95 SLO. Cost estimate: $0.30 / 1k tokens.
- redwood-7b-v1 on H100 (fallback model for long tail): p50=18ms, p95=88ms, p99=190ms. Utility: good lightweight fallback for low-quality-perf tradeoff.

Observed behaviors and anomalies:
- Tail spikes correlated with garbage-collection-like kernel scheduling events on H100 during mixed long/short workloads. When 5% of requests were long (>=512 tokens), p99 for short requests increased by ~2.2x. Root cause appears to be KV cache eviction + dynamic kernel selection thrashing.
- Cold-cache penalty: first-request p95 for short intents on a cold instance measured 550–800ms (primarily due to model weight page-ins and initial kernel JIT). Warm pool reduces that to sub-120ms.
- OOM at high concurrency on A100 when forcing large-batch (>=24) with mixed long sequences; observed memory fragmentation / lack of evictions. Solution: cap forced batch size to 12 for 80GB nodes, prefer continuous batching.
- Quantization artifacts: q4f variant showed occasional hallucination-like formatting differences in structured outputs for long (>300 token) prompts. For short chat intents quality was acceptable.

Cost sensitivity and runbook notes:
- Break-even point: using the dedicated A100 pool with warm cache and batch tuning provides the best cost-quality balance for target workload if steady QPS > 60 req/s per shard. For very bursty low-mean scenarios, the hosted H100 with autoscale and fallback to redwood-7b is better economically.
- Recommendation: primary route short intents to dedicated A100 pool (pinned instances) with prefix cache enabled; offload long or low-priority work to hosted queues with cheaper model variants.
- Autoscaling policy draft: maintain a warm capacity floor equivalent to 20% of peak concurrent players (pre-warmed worker set). Scaling triggers: growth >10% within 60s => add nodes; shrink only after 15m sustained below threshold to avoid churn.

Quality tradeoffs and model routing strategy:
- Primary: redwood-13b-v2 (fp16) — high-quality, good latency when cached and on dedicated.
- Secondary cheaper path: redwood-13b-q4f for non-critical short intents if cost pressure requires; monitor for regression on structured outputs.
- Fallback: redwood-7b-v1 for best-effort low-cost responses; useful for preview/typing indicators where strict fidelity not required.

Operational recommendations and mitigations:
- Implement a prefix-cache-warmup for active sessions: precompute and store KV states for top 3000 active sessions during high-traffic windows. Expected p95 improvement for short intents ~20–30% in steady state.
- Add a kernel-stability monitor that flags repeated kernel-selection changes per instance and automatically restarts the runtime if >5 jitter events occur in 10 minutes. This resolves observed tail anomalies in hosted runs.
- Limit forced-large-batching for mixed-length workloads; prefer continuous batching that respects sequence-length buckets to avoid memory pressure.
- Instrument token-level cost attribution in Redwood Console for Caldera routes so we can show per-scenario unit economics in week-1 post-rollout.

Workshop and customer-facing notes (what to present next):
- Slide 1: TL;DR — A100 dedicated + warm cache meets latency and cost target for Caldera short-intent SLA.
- Slide 2: Test matrix + representative graphs (p95 vs concurrency, cost per 1k tokens vs throughput).
- Slide 3: Anomalies & mitigations (kernel jitter, cold-cache warmup plan).
- Slide 4: Recommended deployment shape and rollout phases (canary -> region ramp -> global).
- Slide 5: Runbook & escalation (who to call: eng-sre oncall, solutions lead, PM).

Next steps and owners:
- Action: Draft a canary rollout plan using a 5% traffic slice to A100 dedicated nodes. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2029-04-19.
- Action: Implement cache warm-up script and add to deploy pipeline (consolidate with infra ops). Owner: Diego Marquez. ETA: 2029-04-15.
- Action: Add kernel-stability metric to Console and create alert. Owner: Evan Zhao. ETA: 2029-04-22.
- Action: Run a 24-hour mixed-workload soak with synthetic long-tail injection (5% long requests) to validate p99 stability. Owner: Jared Bloom. ETA: 2029-04-18.

Open questions / discussion items for next workshop:
- Is Caldera comfortable with the small p99 risk window during long-tail spikes if we deliver lower cost overall? (we should get explicit acceptance for p99 >300ms during 5% long request windows).
- Should the customer prefer dedicated-only for player-facing critical flows, and hosted for maintenance/analytics? Need to clarify contractual SLA expectations.
- Are there regulatory concerns around quantized model variants (any flagged model-qa checks)?

Appendix (raw numbers excerpt for short intent at 600 concurrent):
- H100 hosted (13b fp16, warm): avg qps 92, p50 22ms, p95 98ms, p99 210ms, est cost 0.52/1k
- A100 dedicated (13b fp16, warm): avg qps 88, p50 28ms, p95 115ms, p99 270ms, est cost 0.40/1k
- L4-sim (13b q4f): avg qps 140 (per-dollar high), p50 35ms, p95 145ms, p99 420ms, est cost 0.30/1k

Notes to self (informal):
- Flag: run a focused microbench on kernel selection variance across H100 minor driver revs (we saw better stability on driver x.y.z-3).
- Reminder: attach actual CSVs and latency histograms to Confluence page before customer review.
- Low priority: explore 2-stage routing (preview tokenization step on cheap model then full gen on heavy model) — might cut cost for predictive UI but needs safety checks.

End of doc.
